name: Apache Ignite
tagline: A distributed, memory-first SQL database and compute grid; Ignite 3 rebuilt it around Raft and Calcite.
description: Apache Ignite started as an in-memory data grid and grew into a distributed database with durable native persistence, ANSI SQL, ACID transactions and collocated compute. Ignite 3 (3.0 in 2025, 3.1 in late 2025) is a ground-up rewrite with Raft-based replication, an Apache Calcite SQL engine, schema-first tables and zone-based replication, while the 2.x line (2.18 in April 2026) remains the long-term-support branch most production clusters still run. It suits workloads that need SQL plus key-value access over a sharded, memory-speed dataset, and teams willing to invest in tuning a distributed JVM system.

pricing.notes: Free; commercial support and enterprise features via GridGain.

scale.notes: Partitioned tables across many nodes with optional native persistence; datasets can exceed RAM when persistence is on.

strengths: Distributed ACID transactions and SQL over memory-speed partitions
Collocated compute sends code to the data instead of moving data
Native persistence lets the cluster restart without warming from another store
Ignite 3 brings Raft replication and a Calcite-based SQL planner
weaknesses: Ignite 2 to 3 is a breaking migration with different APIs and storage
Operationally heavy: JVM tuning, rebalancing and baseline topology
Smaller and slower-moving community than it had in the late 2010s
useCases: Accelerating legacy RDBMS with an in-memory SQL cache layer
Distributed caching with SQL queries over cached data
HTAP workloads on a sharded JVM cluster
notIdealFor: Small teams without JVM operations expertise
